why: One segment flip can turn a whole block of zeros into ones, so a window can become all ones if it contains at most max_flips separate runs of zeros. Find the longest window with at most max_flips zero-runs using two pointers.
hints: How many flips does it take to make a window all 1s? Think about blocks of consecutive zeros, not single zeros.
Flipping exactly one maximal block of 0s turns it to 1s without touching anything else, and you can't do better than one flip per block. So a window costs its number of zero-runs.
Slide a window, counting zero-runs inside it (a run starts at a 0 whose left neighbour is a 1 or at the window's left edge); shrink while the count exceeds max_flips. O(n).
pitfalls: Count runs of zeros, not zeros: '1001' needs one flip.
A zero-run cut by the window's left edge still counts as one run.
If max_flips is at least the number of zero-runs, the answer is n.
